cluster_summary: This cluster contains vulnerabilities where WebSocket or HTTP endpoints fail to properly validate the Origin header for cross-origin requests, or where authentication relies on untrusted HTTP headers (proxy-forwarded or user-supplied identifiers) without adequate checks. These flaws enable CSRF bypass, authentication bypass, or unauthorized access.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 2 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Always enforce origin validation for browser-originated requests, regardless of proxy headers. Remove any exemptions that skip origin checks when proxy headers are present..

mechanism.missing_guard: the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect
mechanism.name: Origin validation bypass due to proxy header trust
mechanism.sink_shape: the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs
mechanism.typical_fix: Always enforce origin validation for browser-originated requests, regardless of proxy headers. Remove any exemptions that skip origin checks when proxy headers are present.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Always enforce origin validation for browser-originated requests, regardless of proxy headers. Remove any exemptions that skip origin checks when proxy headers are present.
sub_patterns.name: Origin validation bypass due to proxy header trust
sub_patterns.root_cause: Code assumes that the presence of proxy headers (e.g., X-Forwarded-For) indicates a trusted reverse proxy that has already validated the origin, or trusts proxy-forwarded authentication headers without performing origin checks for browser-originated requests.
